title: Access keys: why they are the last resort, and rotation when unavoidable

videos.script: An access key is two strings. Whoever holds them is that user, from any computer, until somebody deletes the key. {{pair}} It has no second factor. It has no expiry. And it is never guessed. It is copied. {{leaks}} It gets copied into a repository, into an image, into a log, onto a laptop that gets lost. Each of those is a stranger with your key. {{alternatives}} So the first answer is not to have one. The last two lessons gave every machine and every person a way in without a key. This lesson starts by checking that list. {{rotation}} When a key is truly unavoidable, it is rotated. You will create a second key, move the program to it, switch the first one off, wait, and only then delete it. Every step but the last can be undone. {{report}} Then you will read the credential report, the one file that says how old every key in the account is. {{leak}} And last, the day a key leaks. Deactivate it first, find out what it did, and only then replace it. {{end}}
